title: OGA common address model
description: A single address representation that does not lose information across consoles. Flattening every address to one integer is wrong for banked and overlay systems: a SNES address is meaningless without its bank, and an NDS address is meaningless without knowing whether it is a runtime RAM address or an overlay-relative one. Every field here is optional except platform/space/address, so a flat platform only fills what it needs — but the SHAPE is shared, so a tool never has to guess which console it is looking at.

space.description: WHICH address space this is. Never conflate these: a runtime RAM address and a file offset that happen to be equal are different things, and a lossy conversion between them silently produces a wrong answer later.

bank.description: Required for banked systems (GB/GBC, SNES, NES). A banked address does NOT identify code without its bank: the same 16-bit address exists in every bank, so omitting this makes the address ambiguous.

module.description: Module or overlay the address belongs to, e.g. 'arm9/ov000', 'main.elf'. Required when code is dynamically loaded — an overlay-relative address is not a global one.

loadAddress.description: For `virtual`/`runtime-ram` on relocatable code: the base the module was loaded at.

symbol.description: Human/community name for this address, if known. Presence of a name is not evidence the name is correct — pair it with `confidence`.

confidence.description: Honesty marker. Anything not `confirmed` must not be presented as fact downstream.

source.description: Where this mapping came from, so it can be re-checked.

revision.description: Game revision/region this address is valid for. Addresses differ across revisions, so a finding without this is unsafe to reuse.
